sourceLesson: Backend LLD: SOLID Principles for Extensible Systems with AI integrations

questions.title: DIP Versus DI Distinction
questions.question: What is the difference between DIP (Dependency Inversion Principle) and DI (Dependency Injection)?

options.optionText: They are the same thing, just two different names
DIP tells you who to depend on (an abstraction); DI tells you how that dependency reaches you (handed in from outside)
DIP is only for Python; DI is only for other languages
DIP applies to functions; DI applies only to classes

questions.title: Class Explosion With Behaviours
questions.question: If a bird hierarchy has 4 independent behaviours (fly, dance, swim, sing), and you try to model each combination using plain "can/cannot" subclassing, how many classes would you need?

questions.title: Junk Drawer Utility File
questions.question: A project has one utils.py file containing 40 unrelated functions — date logic, string logic, and file logic all mixed together. Which SRP trap is this an example of?

options.optionText: The "does everything" method trap
The "too many if-elif branches" trap
The "junk drawer" utility file trap
This isn't an SRP problem at all

questions.title: Special Handling Signals LSP Break
questions.question: Why does needing a try-except block (or an isinstance check) before calling a method on a subclass count as an LSP violation?

options.optionText: Because try-except blocks are always bad practice in Python - B) Because it means the subclass cannot genuinely be used in place of its
Because it means the subclass cannot genuinely be used in place of its parent without special handling
Because isinstance checks are slower than normal calls
It is not actually an LSP violation

questions.note: Option a) is shown exactly as on the source page, which accidentally includes the start of option b) in it.

questions.title: Static Type Checking Catches Mismatch
questions.question:
With type hints in place, what does a static type checker like mypy do differently from Python itself when this code runs?
```python
flying_things: List[Flyable] = []
flying_things.append(Sparrow())
flying_things.append(Penguin())   # Penguin is NOT a Flyable

for f in flying_things:
    f.fly()
```

options.optionText: mypy prevents the program from running at all, even without being called
mypy would flag flying_things.append(Penguin()) as an error before the program even runs; Python itself only fails when .fly() is actually called on the Penguin, at runtime
mypy and Python behave identically here
mypy only checks syntax, not types like this

questions.title: Notification Service Loop Output

options.optionText: Only "Sending Email: Order shipped!" is printed
Nothing is printed, because NotificationService doesn't create the channels itself
Both "Sending Email: Order shipped!" and "Sending SMS: Order shipped!" are printed, in that order
It raises a TypeError because NotificationChannel is abstract

questions.title: Two Penguin Designs Compared

options.optionText: Both raise the exact same error, so there's no real difference
Design 1 raises NotImplementedError from inside a method that pretends to exist; Design 2 raises AttributeError because fly() was never defined for Penguin at all
Design 1 crashes the program immediately on class creation; Design 2 does not
Design 2 is worse because it gives no error at all

questions.title: Adding New Type Reopens Method

options.optionText: No changes needed — this already supports any future engine type
start() must be reopened and a new elif added for "electric" — this violates OCP
This violates ISP, because Vehicle has too many attributes
This violates DIP, because Vehicle doesn't use inheritance

questions.title: Concrete Payment Gateway Dependency

options.optionText: SRP — checkout() is doing too many jobs
DIP — OrderService depends directly on the concrete RazorpayGateway, and also builds it itself, instead of depending on an abstraction and receiving it from outside
LSP — RazorpayGateway cannot substitute for OrderService
This code has no design issues

questions.title: Adding Channel Without Editing Service
questions.question: A new team wants to add a WhatsAppChannel to a notification system, and they are told they "cannot touch NotificationService directly." If the system was built with one shared abstraction and channels injected from outside (the fixed AI Corner design), what would the new team actually need to do?

options.optionText: Reopen NotificationService and add a new elif branch for WhatsApp
Create a new WhatsAppChannel class implementing the same NotificationChannel abstraction, and pass it into NotificationService from outside
Copy all of NotificationService and rename it
It's impossible to add a new channel without editing NotificationService

questions.title: AI Generated If-Elif Design Flaw
questions.question: An AI assistant was asked to "write a NotificationService using good design principles," and it produced an if-elif chain based on a channel string, inside one send() method. Which principles does this design most clearly fail?

options.optionText: LSP and ISP
OCP, and to some extent SRP
Only DIP
None — "good design principles" was followed correctly

questions.title: Interchangeable Gateways Via Abstraction
questions.question: A checkout system currently uses Razorpay. The business wants to add Stripe next quarter, and possibly switch the default gateway per country later. If the system depends on a PaymentGateway abstraction (not a concrete gateway class), what is the main benefit for this business requirement?

options.optionText: The checkout code doesn't need to change at all when a new gateway is added — only a new gateway class is created
The business would need to rewrite the entire checkout flow for every new gateway
This abstraction only helps with testing, not with adding new gateways
There is no real benefit — hardcoding the gateway is simpler and just as flexible

questions.title: SQLAlchemy Engine Abstraction Example
questions.question: SQLAlchemy's create_engine(url) reads the prefix of a connection string (like postgresql:// or mysql://) and automatically picks the right database driver internally. Which SOLID idea does this real-world example reflect?

options.optionText: SRP only — because create_engine has one function name
The application code depends on a general/abstracted interface, without hardcoding which specific database engine it's talking to — reflecting DIP-style thinking
It reflects LSP only, because databases inherit from each other
It has nothing to do with SOLID — it's just a convenience feature

questions.title: Meaning Of Single Responsibility
questions.question: What does the Single Responsibility Principle (SRP) actually say?

options.optionText: A class should have only one method
A class should have only one reason to change
A class should never inherit from another class
A class should only be used once in the program

questions.title: Open/Closed Principle Extension
questions.question: According to the Open/Closed Principle (OCP), how should you add a new feature to an existing class?

options.optionText: By editing the class directly to add the new behaviour
By adding new code (like a new class), without touching old working code
By deleting the old class and rewriting it from scratch
By adding more if-elif branches inside the same method

questions.title: Substitutability Of Subclasses
questions.question: What does the Liskov Substitution Principle (LSP) require?

options.optionText: A subclass should be replaceable in place of its parent, without breaking the program
A subclass should have more methods than its parent class
A subclass must always override every method of the parent
A subclass should never be used directly in code

questions.title: Interface Segregation Core Idea
questions.question: What is the core idea behind the Interface Segregation Principle (ISP)?

options.optionText: Classes should be forced to implement every method of a shared interface
One large interface is always better than many small ones
A class should not be forced to depend on methods it doesn't actually use
Interfaces should only be used in large-scale applications

questions.title: Dependency Inversion Core Rule
questions.question: What does the Dependency Inversion Principle (DIP) say about two concrete classes?

options.optionText: They should call each other's methods directly for efficiency
They should never depend on each other directly — they should depend on a shared abstraction
They should always be combined into a single class
One concrete class should always inherit from the other

questions.title: Rectangle-Square Substitution Trace

options.optionText: Raises an error

questions.title: Penguin Fly Raises Error

options.optionText: It runs silently, doing nothing
It prints "Penguins can't fly!" and continues normally
It raises a NotImplementedError and crashes the program at that line
It raises a TypeError because Penguin didn't implement fly()

questions.title: Multiple Jobs In One Method
questions.question:
Which SOLID principle does this code violate, and why?
```python
def save_to_database(self):
    connection = connect()
    query = build_query()
    result = run(query, connection)
    obj = map_to_object(result)
    connection.close()
    return obj
```

options.optionText: OCP — because the method can't be extended
SRP — because one method is doing five unrelated jobs (connect, build, run, map, close)
LSP — because it overrides a parent method incorrectly
DIP — because it depends on a concrete database

questions.title: Editing Working Code For New Types

options.optionText: LSP — because eagles and parrots aren't related
ISP — because the method has too many parameters
OCP — because adding a new bird type means editing this already-working method
SRP — because fly() is not a good method name

questions.title: Bundled Interface Forces Fake Method

options.optionText: This violates OCP, because Performable cannot be extended
This violates ISP, because Ostrich is forced to implement fly(), a method it doesn't need
This violates SRP, because Performable has too many method names
This is correct design — no principle is violated

questions.title: Order Processing Multiple Jobs
questions.question: A function process_order() validates the order, charges payment, updates inventory, and sends a confirmation email — all in one function. Which principle does this violate?

options.optionText: SRP
OCP
DIP
ISP

questions.title: Editing Existing Discount Logic
questions.question: A team adds a 6th discount type by adding another elif inside a apply_discount() function that already handles 5 discount types. Which principle is broken?

options.optionText: SRP
OCP
LSP
ISP

questions.title: Fat Interface Forces Fake Methods
questions.question: A Machine abstract class declares print_doc(), scan(), and fax(). A class SimplePrinter inherits from it but only really prints — it raises NotImplementedError for scan() and fax(). Which principle does this violate?

options.optionText: ISP — SimplePrinter is forced to depend on methods it doesn't use
DIP — SimplePrinter depends on a concrete class
LSP — SimplePrinter is not related to Machine
SRP — Machine has too many jobs itself

questions.title: Hardcoded Concrete Dependency
questions.question: Inside OrderService, this line exists: self.gateway = RazorpayGateway(), where RazorpayGateway is a concrete class hardcoded directly. Which principle does this violate?

options.optionText: SRP
OCP
DIP
ISP
